slides.title: How can I make my writing less messy?
slides.body: Let's find out.
slides.notes: Ask: What makes writing look messy? Why do small mistakes matter?

slides.title: Why is this lesson important?
slides.body:
• Most of your writing errors come from punctuation and capitalisation.
  • Fixing these will make your writing clearer and more professional.

slides.title: Instructions
slides.body: Each sentence has errors in punctuation or capitalisation. Circle each error. Write the correction above it.
slides.notes: Demo on the board. Show worksheet task 1.

slides.title: Example
slides.body: i like to read books.
slides.notes: CCQ: Why is 'i' wrong? (Answer: I is always capitalised.)

slides.title: Example
slides.body: I like to read books. The pronoun I is always capitalised.

slides.title: Task 1
slides.body:
Now fix all the errors in questions 1-10.

Question 1 has 2 errors.
slides.notes: Give 8 min. Students work from the worksheet.

slides.title: Question 1 — Spot the error
slides.body: **i** like to learn **english**.

slides.title: Question 1 — Corrected
slides.body: I like to learn English.

slides.title: Question 2 — Spot the error
slides.body: My uncle works as a **Manager**.

slides.title: Question 2 — Corrected
slides.body: My uncle works as a manager.

slides.title: Question 3 — Spot the error
slides.body: She was born in Chiang Mai , Thailand.

slides.title: Question 3 — Corrected
slides.body: She was born in Chiang Mai, Thailand.

slides.title: Question 4 — Spot the error
slides.body: Even though it was raining **W**e went outside.

slides.title: Question 4 — Corrected
slides.body: Even though it was raining, we went outside.

slides.title: Question 5 — Spot the error
slides.body: My best friend who lives next door works as a **Teacher**.

slides.title: Question 5 — Corrected
slides.body: My best friend, who lives next door, works as a teacher.

slides.title: Question 6 — Spot the error
slides.body: In my opinion **T**he school needs a new library.

slides.title: Question 6 — Corrected
slides.body: In my opinion, the school needs a new library.

slides.title: Question 7 — Spot the error
slides.body: My friend Anna likes to play football.

slides.title: Question 7 — Corrected
slides.body: My friend, Anna, likes to play football.

slides.title: Question 8 — Spot the error
slides.body: I was tired but I kept studying.

slides.title: Question 8 — Corrected
slides.body: I was tired, but I kept studying.

slides.title: Question 9 — Spot the error
slides.body: I wanted to go to the party however I was sick.

slides.title: Question 9 — Corrected
slides.body: I wanted to go to the party; however, I was sick.

slides.title: Question 10 — Spot the error
slides.body: Many **Students** like to play games at break time.

slides.title: Question 10 — Corrected
slides.body: Many students like to play games at break time.

slides.title: Task 2 — Recall
slides.body: Each box shows an error from Task 1. Explain the rule that was broken. Write **one complete sentence**.
slides.notes: Give 5 min. Demo: 'i' → 'The pronoun I must always be capitalised.'

slides.title: Rule — Common nouns
slides.body: Don't capitalise common nouns. Only proper nouns (names, places) need capitals. teacher, manager, students → lowercase.
slides.notes: CCQ: Is 'English' a common or proper noun? (Proper — language name.)

slides.title: Rule 1 — Comma spacing
slides.body: Never put a space **before** a comma. Always put a space **after** a comma. Chiang Mai, Thailand ✓
slides.notes: CCQ: Which is correct: 'word , word' or 'word, word'?

slides.title: Rule 2 — Extra information
slides.body: Use **commas** around extra information about a person. My friend, Anna, likes football.
slides.notes: CCQ: If we remove 'Anna', is the sentence still complete? (Yes.)

slides.title: Rule 3 — After an introduction
slides.body: After an introductory phrase, use a **comma**. Then use a **lowercase** letter. In my opinion, the school ✓
slides.notes: CCQ: What comes after the comma? A lowercase letter.

slides.title: Rule 4 — Connecting with **However**
slides.body: Use a **semicolon** before **however**. Use a **comma** after it. ...the party ; however, I was sick.
slides.notes: CCQ: What goes BEFORE 'however'? A semicolon. What goes AFTER? A comma.

slides.title: Task 3 — Use
slides.body:
Write a paragraph about **a fun day** with your family or friends.

Focus on correct punctuation and capitalisation.

Up to 70 words.

slides.title: Checklist
slides.body:
• A sentence starting with while or even though
  • A sentence with extra information in commas
  • Correct comma before and or but
  • The word however used correctly
slides.notes: Review each item. Ask for example sentences.
